Lonzo Anderson Ball was born on October 27, 1997.
Lonzo Anderson Ball is an American professional basketball player.
Lonzo Anderson Ball plays for the Chicago Bulls of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Lonzo Anderson Ball is a point guard.
Lonzo Anderson Ball played college basketball for one season with the UCLA Bruins.
Lonzo Anderson Ball earned consensus first-team All-American honors during his college career.
The Los Angeles Lakers selected Lonzo Anderson Ball with the second overall pick of the 2017 NBA draft.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team in 2018.
As a high school senior at Chino Hills High School in 2016, Lonzo Anderson Ball led his team to an undefeated 35-0 record and consensus national top ranking alongside brothers LiAngelo and LaMelo.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was awarded multiple national high school player of the year honors as a high school senior at Chino Hills High School in 2016.
Lonzo Anderson Ball played basketball at Chino Hills High School in Chino Hills, California.
Lonzo Anderson Ball averaged 25 points, 11 rebounds, 9.1 assists, and 5 blocks per game during his junior year at Chino Hills High School in 2014-15.
Lonzo Anderson Ball led the school to a state title as a senior in 2016.
Lonzo Anderson Ball's younger brothers LiAngelo and LaMelo were also on the team with him during their high school years.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was rated as a consensus five-star recruit in the 2016 high school class.
Lonzo Anderson Ball signed a National Letter of Intent to attend UCLA, committing to play for the Bruins.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was one of 50 players named to the preseason watch list for the John R. Wooden Award in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball and T.J. Leaf helped UCLA bounce back from a 15-17 record to a 31-5 record during his freshman season in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball led the nation in assists as a freshman at UCLA in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball transformed the Bruins into the top scoring offense in the country as a freshman in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had 22 points, six rebounds, and five assists against Washington Huskies on February 4, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was named MVP of the Wooden Legacy tournament after leading UCLA to a win over Texas A&M in the championship game during his freshman season in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had a career-high 14 assists against Washington State on March 3, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball broke Gary Payton's 30-year-old Pac-12 season record for assists by a freshman with his performance against Washington State in 2016-17.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had 15 points and three assists to surpass Larry Drew II's school record for most assists in a season during the NCAA tournament in 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball came close to a triple-double with 18 points, seven rebounds, and nine assists against Cincinnati in the second round of the NCAA tournament in 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had 10 points, eight assists, and four turnovers during his performance against Kentucky in the Sweet 16 of the NCAA tournament in 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball declared for the 2017 NBA draft after the season ended in 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was projected to be a top-3 pick in the 2017 NBA draft by various sources.
Lonzo Anderson Ball played in 52 games during his rookie season with the Lakers in 2017-18, missing 30 due to injuries.
Lonzo Anderson Ball scored a career-high 29 points against the Phoenix Suns on October 20, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had eight points, eight rebounds, and 13 assists against the New Orleans Pelicans in his second game of the season on October 22, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball recorded a triple-double with 19 points, 13 assists, and 12 rebounds against the Milwaukee Bucks on November 11, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball missed the team's Christmas game after spraining his left shoulder in the previous game against the Portland Trail Blazers on December 25, 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball returned to play after missing six games due to a knee injury against the Dallas Mavericks on January 13, 2018.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was selected to play in the Rising Stars Challenge during NBA All-Star Weekend but withdrew because of his injury on February 19, 2018.
Lonzo Anderson Ball missed the final eight games of the season due to a knee contusion and ended the season with averages of 10.2 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.9 rebounds in 2017-18.
Lonzo Anderson Ball underwent an arthroscopic surgery on his left knee to repair a torn meniscus on July 17, 2018.
The Lakers signed LeBron James during the offseason of 2018, which shifted the spotlight away from Lonzo Anderson Ball.
Rajon Rondo was signed by the Lakers to mentor and compete with Lonzo Anderson Ball in 2018.
Lonzo Anderson Ball made his debut for the New Orleans Pelicans on October 22, 2018, registering eight points, five rebounds, and five assists against the Toronto Raptors.
Lonzo Anderson Ball hit a career-high seven three-pointers and scored a season-high 27 points in a win over the Houston Rockets on December 29, 2018.
Lonzo Anderson Ball recorded his first triple-double of the season with 18 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists against the Los Angeles Clippers on January 18, 2019.
Lonzo Anderson Ball matched his career-high seven three-pointers while recording 26 points and eight assists in a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on March 3, 2019.
Lonzo Anderson Ball also made seven three-pointers against the Dallas Mavericks the following day, finishing with 25 points, 11 rebounds, and six assists in an overtime loss.
From December 2019 to March 2020, Lonzo Anderson Ball averaged 12.7 points, 7.3 assists, and 6.7 rebounds while shooting 39.2% from three during a 45-game span.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was at his healthiest heading into the 2020-21 season.
Stan Van Gundy placed Lonzo Anderson Ball in a 3-and-D role for the Pelicans, which he had never played before.
On January 29, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball matched his career-high seven three-pointers and scored a season-high 27 points against the Bucks.
On April 5, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball set a new career-high with eight three-pointers while matching his season-high 27 points and registering nine assists in a win over the Rockets.
On May 1, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball matched his career-high eight three-pointers while recording a career-high 33 points alongside 11 rebounds and eight assists against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Lonzo Anderson Ball ended the season with career highs in scoring (14.6), 3-point percentage (37.8%), field goal percentage (41.4) and free throw percentage (78.1).
Lonzo Anderson Ball was a restricted free agent during the offseason of 2021.
On August 8, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball was traded to the Chicago Bulls in a sign-and-trade deal with the Pelicans receiving Tomáš Satoranský, Garrett Temple and draft picks.
Lonzo Anderson Ball signed a four-year, $85 million contract extension with the Bulls on August 8, 2021.
On October 20, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball made his debut for the Chicago Bulls in a win over the Detroit Pistons.
On October 22, 2021, Lonzo Anderson Ball recorded a triple-double with 17 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists against the New Orleans Pelicans.
Lonzo Anderson Ball underwent arthroscopic debridement surgery on his left knee in August 2021 to treat recurring discomfort during rehabilitation when his physical activity was increased.
On January 20, 2022, Lonzo Anderson Ball missed three games with a meniscus tear and was expected to undergo surgery and miss six to eight weeks.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was ruled out for the remainder of the 2021-22 season after experiencing pain during rehabilitation when his physical activity was increased on April 6, 2022.
Lonzo Anderson Ball played in 35 games in the 2021-22 season, the fewest in his career.
The Chicago Bulls announced that Lonzo Anderson Ball would undergo surgery on his left knee and miss six to eight weeks after missing three games with a meniscus tear on January 20, 2022.
Lonzo Anderson Ball was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to pain during rehabilitation when his physical activity was increased on April 6, 2022.

Lonzo Anderson Ball did not appear in any NBA games since January 2022 due to a knee injury and it appeared he would attempt to return to the court in 2024-25 despite missing two whole seasons as of June 26, 2024.
In July 2024, Lonzo Anderson Ball was cleared to participate in full-contact five-on-five scrimmages.
In August 2024, Lonzo Anderson Ball began participating in these scrimmages and has experienced no setbacks.
Lonzo Anderson Ball formerly had an unorthodox jump shot that involved moving the ball from his left hip to the left of his forehead before shooting towards the basket.
Lonzo Anderson Ball preferred to shoot jumpers while moving towards his left.
Lonzo Anderson Ball averaged only 31% shooting from three-point range in his two seasons with the Lakers.
Lonzo Anderson Ball began shooting in a more conventional form, squaring up the ball to his forehead, during the 2020-21 NBA season.
Lonzo Anderson Ball began shooting in games from 40 feet deep when he was a pre-teen.
Lonzo Anderson Ball shot three-pointers from beyond the NBA line during college, which is 4 feet longer than the 19-foot-9-inch college line.
Lonzo Anderson Ball's go-to shot with time expiring was a step-back three-pointer from deep.
Lonzo Anderson Ball began his pro career using sports apparel from his father LaVar's Big Baller Brand instead of signing with any major apparel companies.
Lonzo Anderson Ball's father, LaVar, insisted that he not sign with a company unless they agreed to license merchandise from Big Baller Brand.
On May 16, 2017, Big Baller Brand announced the release of Lonzo Anderson Ball's first shoe, the ZO2.
The $495 price tag on the ZO2 sparked wide criticism from celebrities and social media regarding its potential quality in comparison to competing brands such as Nike and Adidas.
Lonzo Anderson Ball owned 51% of Big Baller Brand while his father LaVar owned 16.4%, and both his mother Tina and Alan Foster, co-founder of Big Baller Brand, each owned 16.3%.
Jordan Crawford became the first player besides Lonzo Anderson Ball to wear the ZO2s during a game on April 6, 2018.

On December 20, 2017, Lonzo Anderson Ball was announced as the logo for the Junior Basketball Association (JBA), a league his father LaVar planned to establish for high-school basketball players who have finished high school but want an alternative option to the NCAA.
Lonzo Anderson Ball's mother Tina suffered a stroke and was hospitalized for two months in December 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball had a long-term relationship with Denise García, with whom he has a daughter.
Lonzo Anderson Ball released his first rap single "Melo Ball 1" as an ode to his youngest brother LaMelo in September 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball released the song "ZO2", dedicated to his own brand of shoes, during that same month in September 2017.
Lonzo Anderson Ball released another rap single titled "Super Saiyan" in February 2018, which compared himself to Goku from Dragon Ball Z.
On February 15, 2018, Lonzo Anderson Ball and his father LaVar participated in the Lip Sync Battle as competitors.
On February 15, 2018, Lonzo Anderson Ball released his debut album "Born 2 Ball" under the name Zo.
The album was released under the Big Baller Music Group, a subsidiary of the Big Baller Brand run by a close friend of LaVar.
"Born 2 Ball" peaked at No. 42 on Billboard's Independent Albums chart and No. 13 on its Heatseekers Albums chart in March 2018.
Lonzo Anderson Ball competed on the fourth season of The Masked Singer as "Whatchamacallit" in 2020, where he was eliminated alongside Dr. Elvis Francois as "Serpent".
Lonzo Anderson Ball and his family premiered their own Facebook Watch reality show called "Ball in the Family" in August 2019.
